subject.title: Feature: Floating agent bubbles (Clawi) for macOS

question: Should OpenClaw ship persistent per-agent floating bubbles as a first-party native macOS interaction surface?
rationale: The missing behavior is clear, but implementation depends on maintainer intent for a prominent desktop interaction, accessibility and click-through semantics, persistence ownership, multi-Space lifecycle, and agent-to-session routing.

options.title: Design first-party bubbles
options.body: Keep this issue as the product-design owner and define the native interaction, state, accessibility, and routing contract before implementation.

options.title: Defer the surface
options.body: Keep the current menu-bar HUD and native WebChat as the supported interaction and close the bubble concept if it is not a current companion-app priority.

options.title: Design an extension seam
options.body: Create a supported native macOS UI/window extension boundary only if maintainers want the bubble experience to be externally owned.

recommendation.title: Design first-party bubbles
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the product-design owner and define the native interaction, state, accessibility, and routing contract before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the native macOS app, remain the strongest recent contributor across the adjacent HUD/activity/chat surfaces, and already reviewed this issue's product boundary.
